summary: Tested read receipts (backend WS and REST, plus ChatPage ticks) and the photo-thumbnail/Likes-skeleton/prefetch changes. Backend: 11/11 pytest pass. (1) Receiver online, REST send: the sender gets message_delivered with the right message_id and the DB has delivered=true. mark-read then sends messages_read (read_by=B) and the DB has read=true and delivered=true. (2) The WS send path also gives delivered and the receiver gets the message event. (3) Receiver offline: no delivered event and delivered stays false. When B connects WS, the sender gets message_delivered with all:true and the DB is updated. (4) AI receiver (Sara Mehta): delivered arrives immediately and messages_read about 3.6s later. /api/likes, /api/matches, /api/conversations and /api/chat/{id}/info have no data:image. Profile pictures carry &w=400 and photos &w=720. The thumbnail at /api/photo/4fc1d920.../p?w=400 is 22.7KB vs the 843KB original. The v hash from /api/likes (Mongo marker path) equals the md5 computed from the full base64 value, so it is consistent with the other endpoints. /api/discover/{id} returns 200. Frontend (390x844): login works. likes-skeleton renders on first load with empty cache, then content shows. Discover does not crash when hl_discover_{uid} and hl_discover_cache_{uid} hold objects. Likes, Matches and Chat pages have 0 broken images and 0 page errors. Chat with the AI match: the tick goes clock, then grey CheckCheck (0.1s), then blue CheckCheck rgb(79,195,247) at 2.1s, and stays blue after reload.

minor.issue: Pre-existing: no authentication. Anyone can connect as any user_id, receive that user's messages and trigger delivered acks or _deliver_pending for them.

Only one socket is kept per user, and disconnect(user_id) deletes it by key without checking which socket closed. If an old socket closes after a reconnect (or a second tab/device closes), the live connection is removed. The receiver then looks offline, so ticks stay as a single check until the next connect. Fix: disconnect(user_id, websocket) and only delete if it is the same socket, or keep a set of sockets per user.
Pre-existing: no auth or ownership check.
Runs an aggregate on messages {receiver_id, delivered:{$ne:true}} on every WS connect. Add a compound index (receiver_id, delivered) to keep it cheap.
Returns 401 about 5 times on every page load for the admin user (frontend calls it without auth or with the wrong auth). Log noise only.

integration_issues.issue: Minor race: if a message_delivered or messages_read WS event arrives before the REST response replaces the temp message, the replacement (response.data with delivered=false) can bring the tick back down until the next event.

issues: The DailyRewardModal (data-testid daily-reward-modal) pops up over an open chat about 2-3s after it loads, even after it was closed once, and blocks the send button. This made one test message silently fail to send. Consider suppressing it on /chat routes.

action_items: Make ConnectionManager.disconnect socket-aware (or keep multiple sockets per user) so stale socket closes don't mark an online receiver offline. This directly affects delivered ticks.
Optional: add a db.messages index on (receiver_id, delivered).
Optional: suppress DailyRewardModal on the chat route; fix the repeated 401s from /api/admin/feature-flags.
Pre-existing security: authenticate the WS and mark-read endpoints.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 12.3k lines; split it into routers (messages/ws, photos, likes).

_ack_message for AI marks all unread messages in the match as read with update_many, which is correct. Delivered for real users depends on the in-process manager.active_connections, which only works with --workers 1. Multi-worker production would need Redis pub/sub.
Message model has no delivered or read defaults, so old docs lack the field (the frontend treats missing as false, which is fine).
DiscoverPage.fetchProfiles does setProfiles(response.data) without an Array.isArray guard. If the API ever returns an object, the page breaks.

rca of the issue: Ticks: before this change the backend never set delivered or emitted message_delivered. It now does so via _ack_message (on send) and _deliver_pending (on WS connect), and the frontend handles both events. Verified working.
